Gaussian process spatial structure (NNGP)

Source: R/spatial_gp.R
spatial_gp.Rd

Specify a Gaussian-process spatial random effect, approximated with a nearest-neighbour GP (NNGP) for scalability. Captures smooth spatial variation from point-referenced coordinates.

Usage

spatial_gp(
  coords,
  approx = c("nngp", "hsgp"),
  cov = NULL,
  nu = 1.5,
  nn = 15,
  m = NULL,
  c = NULL,
  sigma_prior_U = 1,
  sigma_prior_alpha = 0.01,
  shared = NULL,
  scale_coords = TRUE,
  parameterization = c("auto", "noncentered", "centered", "collapsed")
)

# S3 method for class 'tulpa_gp'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tulpa_hsgp'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

coords

A formula (~ lon + lat) or character vector naming the coordinate variables in the data. With approx = "nngp" the coordinate DIMENSION is however many are named: two for a map, one for a transect or a depth profile, three for a depth-resolved domain. The neighbour graph and the neighbour covariance both read every column. approx = "hsgp" takes exactly two, and so does any sampler mode, because both store coordinates at a fixed 2-D stride.

approx

GP approximation: "nngp" (default, a nearest-neighbour GP with the cov / nu / nn arguments) or "hsgp" (a Hilbert-space basis GP with m functions per dimension and boundary factor c, which approximates the kernel cov / nu name).

cov

Covariance function. With approx = "nngp", "exponential" (the default) or "matern". With approx = "hsgp", "matern" (the default, at nu = 1.5) or "squared_exponential"; the exponential kernel has no HSGP basis rule. NULL takes the approximation's default.

nu

Matern smoothness parameter, one of 1.5 or 2.5. Used only when cov = "matern" (nu = 0.5 is cov = "exponential").

nn

Number of nearest neighbours used in the NNGP approximation.

m

Number of HSGP basis functions per dimension (approx = "hsgp"), between 3 and 50. NULL (default) chooses it from the data; see Details.

c

HSGP boundary factor, >= 1 (approx = "hsgp"): the basis lives on the coordinates' bounding box widened by c. NULL (default) chooses it from the data; see Details.

sigma_prior_U, sigma_prior_alpha

Penalized-complexity prior on the field's marginal standard deviation (approx = "hsgp"), calibrated so that P(sigma > sigma_prior_U) = sigma_prior_alpha. Defaults to P(sigma > 1) = 0.01. sigma_prior_U must be positive and sigma_prior_alpha must lie in (0, 1). Sampler and nested-Laplace routes use these anchors. Under hyperprior = "flat", nested Laplace retains explicitly supplied anchors.

shared

Whether the spatial effect is shared across processes in a multi-process model. NULL (default) shares the effect; FALSE fits process-specific effects and emits a warning.

scale_coords

Logical. Standardize coordinates before fitting (default TRUE): each column is centred and all are divided by one common factor, so distances keep their proportions and an isotropic kernel stays isotropic. spatial_range() reports the range in the original coordinate units either way.

parameterization

Latent parameterization for the exact-NUTS field. "auto" scales covariance-whitened coordinates using prior and observation information. "noncentered" samples z ~ N(0, I) and reconstructs the field as w = f(z, sigma2, phi). "centered" samples field values. "collapsed" analytically integrates a Gaussian-likelihood NNGP field under NUTS/HMC and returns exact conditional field draws. Non-Gaussian collapsing is refused; use "auto" for full-field NUTS.

x

A tulpa_gp or tulpa_hsgp specification.

...

Ignored.

Value

A tulpa_gp object (also of class tulpa_spatial).

Details

HSGP kernel. The basis approximates a Matern kernel of smoothness 3/2 (the default) or 5/2, sigma^2 (1 + sqrt(3) d / ell) exp(-sqrt(3) d / ell) and sigma^2 (1 + sqrt(5) d / ell + 5 d^2 / (3 ell^2)) exp(-sqrt(5) d / ell) at distance d, or the squared-exponential kernel sigma^2 exp(-d^2 / (2 ell^2)), through each kernel's spectral density (Riutort-Mayol et al. 2023, Eqs. 1-3). The squared-exponential kernel draws fields smoother than any Matern one, and a field rougher than the kernel assumes is smoothed and its intervals narrowed.

For nested Laplace and Hamiltonian inference, the default PC (penalised complexity) prior places half its probability below an effective range of one fifth of the coordinate bounding-box diagonal. The effective range is rho = 2 * ell, where ell is the kernel lengthscale (phi in the NNGP kernels). Both approximations use this anchor. spatial_multiscale() takes each scale's anchor from its declared range interval.

HSGP basis size. A Hilbert-space basis of m functions per dimension on a domain widened by c has a lower lengthscale cutoff a c max(S) / m, where S contains the coordinate half-widths and c >= 1.2. The coefficient a retains 99% of the joint two-dimensional spectral variance using the tensor expansion and cumulative-variance recommendation of Riutort-Mayol et al. (2023, Eqs. 9-12, Section 4.2). It is at least their one-dimensional covariance-error coefficient (Eqs. 19, 21, 23). The boundary factor follows Eqs. 20, 22, 24 and bounds the variance removed by the Dirichlet boundary at the domain's corners by 1%, using the kernel correlations at twice the distance to each face. A rough field asks for a short lengthscale, and a basis too small for it smooths the field and narrows its intervals. Left unset, m and c follow the iterative procedure of the paper's Section 4.5.1. In its Phase A the first fit takes them from the prior median of the lengthscale, and while the posterior median lengthscale falls below the smallest one the fitted basis represents (the paper's diagnostic, with its slack of 0.01 on the lengthscale divided by S), the field is fitted again with the m and c that estimate asks for. In its Phase B five functions per dimension are added and the field fitted again until the refit passes the diagnostic and is stable against the fit before it: the paper names the lengthscale estimate and the predictive accuracy as what has to be stable and gives no threshold, and stable is read here as the refitted posterior mean of the lengthscale, and of the linear predictor at every observation, lying inside the previous fit's 95% interval. m never shrinks below a size already fitted and stops at 50. A supplied m or c is kept as given, and a supplied m ends the procedure after Phase A. diagnostics() reports when the posterior median lengthscale lies outside the window of the fitted basis at either end; above it, the field is smoother than the boundary factor allows for, and a larger c covers it.

References

Riutort-Mayol, G., Buerkner, P.-C., Andersen, M. R., Solin, A. and Vehtari, A. (2023). Practical Hilbert space approximate Bayesian Gaussian processes for probabilistic programming. Statistics and Computing 33, 17. doi:10.1007/s11222-022-10167-2

See also

spatial_car(), spatial_bym2() for areal spatial effects.

Examples

# GP spatial specification from coordinate columns
spatial_gp(~ lon + lat)
#> tulpa Gaussian Process spatial specification
#> =============================================
#> 
#> Coordinates: lon, lat 
#> Covariance: exponential 
#> Neighbors (NNGP): 15 
#> Shared: Yes (enters both processes) 
spatial_gp(~ lon + lat, cov = "matern", nu = 1.5)
#> tulpa Gaussian Process spatial specification
#> =============================================
#> 
#> Coordinates: lon, lat 
#> Covariance: matern (nu = 1.5) 
#> Neighbors (NNGP): 15 
#> Shared: Yes (enters both processes) 
spatial_gp(~ lon + lat, approx = "hsgp", cov = "squared_exponential")
#> tulpa Hilbert Space GP (HSGP) spatial specification
#> =====================================================
#> 
#> Coordinates: lon, lat 
#> Kernel: squared exponential 
#> Basis functions: chosen from the data
#> Boundary factor: chosen from the data
#> Shared: Yes (enters both processes)
